chg.title: What changed for tax year {year}

items.title: Child tax credit eligibility
items.desc: For tax years 2026–2029 only children born in 2016 or earlier qualify (2017 births are excluded due to the expanded child allowance). From tax year 2030: age 13 and over.

items.title: Higher card deduction limit for parents
items.desc: The basic limit rises by 500,000 KRW per child, up to 1M KRW. Above 70M KRW salary: 250,000 KRW per child, up to 500,000 KRW.

items.title: Arts & sports academies for grades 1–2
items.desc: Arts, music and sports academy fees for 1st and 2nd graders now qualify for the education credit (15%, up to 3M KRW per child).

items.title: No income test for dependants' education costs
items.desc: From education costs paid on or after 1 January 2026, a dependant's age and income no longer matter — tuition for a university student child earning over ₩1M from part-time work now counts (parents' and grandparents' education costs are still excluded).

items.title: Rent credit extended to spouses
items.desc: Rent paid by the spouse of an eligible household head now qualifies (couple combined up to 10M KRW a year).

items.title: Marriage credit ends soon
items.desc: Couples registering marriage in 2024–2026 get 500,000 KRW each (once per lifetime). Registrations must be made by December 31, 2026.

yt.sources: Basis: Income Tax Act §47, §55, §59–59-4 (amended 2025-12-23 and 2026-04-21); Restriction of Special Taxation Act §30, 58, 87, 92, 95-2, 126-2 (amended 2025-12-23). Current law as of 2026-10-04 (law.go.kr). 2026 insurance rates.

tips.title: Tax-saving tips
items: Use credit cards up to 25% of salary, then debit/cash receipts (30% rate).
Markets, transit (40%) and books/shows/gyms (30%) share an extra 3M KRW limit (2M above 70M salary).
Pension/IRP contributions count if paid by Dec 31 (up to 9M KRW, 15% or 12%).
Medical costs only count above 3% of salary — dual earners should use the lower earner.
If your final tax is already 0, extra deductions add nothing — give dependents to the higher-tax spouse.

whatIs.title: What is the Year-End Tax Calculator?
whatIs.description: This tool estimates your year-end tax settlement refund (or additional payment). Enter gross salary, personal deductions, social insurance, card spending, pension savings, medical/education expenses to calculate your final tax and refund amount.

howToUse.title: How to use
items: Enter just your salary to see a result with realistic defaults (single, card spending).
Open family, cards, pension, medical and other sections as needed — results update instantly.
For accuracy, enter the income tax withheld from your payslips or withholding receipt.
Check 'Ways to get more back' for moves you can still make before Dec 31.

items.q: When do I receive my refund?
items.a: Usually reflected in February salary. Additional tax due is deducted from salary.

items.q: Income deduction vs tax credit - what's the difference?
items.a: Income deductions reduce your taxable income base, while tax credits directly reduce the calculated tax amount. Tax credits have a more direct impact.
Spouse (income under 1M KRW), parents (age 60+), children (under 20 or disabled), siblings (under 20 or 60+, income under 1M KRW).
